review.note: Drafted by the assistant in M44b under the owner's dated exception, from the sources named and not from a reading of them; the argument is the thing to check, not only the dates.

explanation: The Munich putsch of November 1923 tried to do what Rome had done thirteen months earlier, and its organisers said so. The plan was to seize Bavaria and march on Berlin as Mussolini had marched on Rome. The failure taught the party a lesson it acted on for the next ten years, that it had to arrive at power rather than seize it. The edge claims the model and the intention. The outcome was the opposite of the Italian one.
